report:
**Conclusion: supported.** In the pivotal randomized ACTIVE trial, daily subcutaneous abaloparatide for 18 months reduced new vertebral fractures in postmenopausal women with osteoporosis versus placebo. FDA labeling reports new vertebral fractures in **0.6%** of abaloparatide-treated women versus **4.2%** with placebo (*p*<0.0001)—an absolute reduction of about 3.6 percentage points and relative reduction of about 86%. The trial publication likewise concludes that abaloparatide reduced new vertebral and nonvertebral fractures over 18 months.

This evidence applies most directly to postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at elevated fracture risk, rather than all women or prevention in those without osteoporosis. Clinical guidance recommends abaloparatide (up to two years) for postmenopausal women at **very high** fracture risk, including those with severe or multiple vertebral fractures.
